Risk call on GAKU: lean refuse, but if the desk insists, minimum size.

Pool depth is only 74.86 SOL, and the coin is 68% off its 30-minute high with 30 min of heavy net selling in the last window (sell SOL 147 vs buy 175, sellers outnumber buyers). The curve shows a 50% bundle share and a launch bot, which matches neither a clean organic launch nor an operator-backed one. Round-trip slippage on a $20 ticket here is likely at the top of the 1.4-5.1% range.

If the desk buys anyway: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 15-30 min hold, exit on any further drawdown. Refuse at any size if the stop can't be placed before the 30-second fill lag, if pool depth falls further, or if the sell-to-buy ratio stays above 1.
memos.scout:
Honest case for buying GAKU now: weak, and I don't think it clears the bar.

What the brief supports: it's alive, classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump, and the last 15 minutes show net positive flow (+27.6 SOL, 461 buyers against 352 sellers) and a 1.14x return. The top-3 holder share is low at 7.4%, and the first two minutes after graduation drew 426 buyers with only 0.88 sell-to-buy, so early demand was real.

What argues against it: half the curve (50.4%) was bundle-bought, which is a strong sign of coordinated rather than organic demand. The coin sits 68% below its 30-minute high and is down 25% over 30 minutes, so the recent 15-minute bounce is a dip recovery of a kind the base rates say usually fails. Sell-side volume of 147 SOL against 175 SOL of buys means the bounce is being sold into. The pool is thin at 75 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces the high end of the 1.4-5.1% cost range, and a bundled, half-retraced coin gives little reason to expect follow-through in 30-60 minutes.

Verdict: no strong case. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is a late-stage distribution that the "ORGANIC" label hides. The first two minutes after graduation show 238.98 SOL bought against a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.88, so early demand was largely recycled into exits, and a launch bot was present. Over the last 15 minutes, sell volume (147.38 SOL) nearly matched buys (175.01 SOL) with 352 sellers against 461 buyers, and net flow of only 27.63 SOL is thin for a $36.7k market cap. The bundle share of 0.5038 means half the curve came from coordinated wallets, which is a common setup for insiders exiting into retail. The price is already down 68% from the 30-minute high, so a bounce must overcome fees of 1.4-5.1% and a shallow 74.86 SOL pool. My verdict is skip: the numbers point to distribution and dead volume rather than a clean entry.
